title: Daily Dose #374: Work for the Lord
body:
**“Whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord and not for men.”**

Not every task feels important. Some work is repetitive, unnoticed or far from what we hoped we would be doing.

Paul wrote to people whose daily work was often controlled by others, yet he gave them a higher audience: the Lord. This does not excuse exploitation or poor treatment. It means no honest work is beneath faithfulness when it is offered to Christ.

Working for the Lord changes the standard when supervision is absent. It challenges laziness, dishonesty and the need for constant praise. It also protects us from making human approval our master.

Do the next task well. Treat people fairly. Keep your word. If the work is harmful or dishonest, seek a way out rather than calling compromise faithfulness.

The Lord sees the work others overlook.
